result.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
result.comment: Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
result.summary: AI systems must often maintain bounded memory of unbounded interaction histories. However, optimizing the memory representation, and its updates, for downstream task utility is difficult for standard reinforcement learning (RL) due to severe credit assignment bottlenecks induced by sparse, delayed rewards. We introduce MaxIM (Maximally Informative Incremental Memory), a framework that formulates incremental summarization as a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping problem. Grounded in value suboptimality bounds, we show that bounding sequential information loss motivates maximizing the predictive log-likelihood of future, task-relevant targets, a variational lower bound on predictive sufficiency. We introduce a recursive consistency condition to ensure summaries are grounded by maximizing mutual information (MI) with the observed history. We mitigate credit assignment issues with a parameterized asymmetric critic that computes step-wise variational MI bounds for dense reward shaping. Empirical evaluation on long-horizon scientific reading and multi-turn dialogue benchmarks shows that MaxIM outperforms RL, supervised fine-tuning, and prompt-focused baselines on factual grounding, comprehensive autorater metrics, and downstream task utility across strict token budgets and extended horizons, without the need for expensive human preference labels.

AI.brief_summary: MaxIM 将无界交互历史的增量摘要建模为容量受限的记忆更新问题，以预测未来任务相关目标的变分下界和互信息一致性构造信息论奖励，并用非对称 critic 提供稠密奖励，缓解稀疏延迟奖励下的信用分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以任务可用信息约束记忆、用稠密互信息奖励训练状态更新的思路，可能为 LVR 中 latent 视觉状态的筛选、信息坍缩诊断及稀疏答案奖励下的贡献分配提供可核查线索。
